s:
Consider the following statements about recognition as a national party:
1. The conditions are laid down in Paragraph 6B of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.
2. Under one route, 6% of valid votes in four or more States and at least 4 Lok Sabha seats are both mandatory.
3. Under another route, a party must win 2% of the Lok Sabha seats (11 of 543) with members elected from at least four States.
4. A party recognised as a State party in four or more States qualifies as a national party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 2% route (11 of 543 seats) needs members elected from at least three States, not four. Fulfilling any one of the three conditions is enough.

Match List-I (Date) with List-II (Number of national parties):
List-I | List-II
a. 1952 (first Lok Sabha) | i. 8
b. 1999 general election | ii. 14
c. May 2020 | iii. 7
d. After the review of 10 April 2023 | iv. 6
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 1952 – 14 national (39 State) parties; 1999 – 7 national, 40 State (ECI); May 2020 – eight (NPP added in June 2019); after the 10 April 2023 review – six: BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP, AAP.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National People's Party of Meghalaya, recognised in June 2019, was the first party from the North-East to get national status.
2. In the April 2023 review the AAP was recognised as a national party while the NCP and AITC lost that status.
3. The CPI(M) also lost its national-party status in the April 2023 review.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the parties derecognised in April 2023 were the CPI, NCP and AITC; the CPI(M) remains one of the six national parties (BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP, AAP).

s:
Which of the following parties have never been recognised as a national party?
1. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
2. Telugu Desam Party
3. Samajwadi Party
4. All India Trinamool Congress
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: 1, 2 and 3 have never been national parties (nor have the RSP, AIFB and Peasants and Workers Party; TDP and YSRCP are recognised State parties in AP). 4 is wrong: the AITC got national status on 2 September 2016 and lost it in April 2023.

s:
Consider the following statements about the registration of political parties:
1. Registration under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951 and recognition under the Symbols Order, 1968 are both done by the Election Commission of India.
2. A new party must apply for registration within 60 days of its formation.
3. The party's constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism and democracy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the application must be made within 30 days of formation.

Match List-I (Provision) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Paragraph 6B, Symbols Order 1968 | i. Conditions for national-party recognition
b. Paragraph 15, Symbols Order 1968 | ii. Suspension or withdrawal of recognition for defying the Model Code of Conduct
c. Paragraph 16A, Symbols Order 1968 | iii. Registration of political parties
d. Section 29A, RPA 1951 | iv. Split disputes decided by the Sadiq Ali majority test
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Para 6B – national-party criteria; Para 15 – split disputes over name and symbol (Sadiq Ali, 1971: majority support of the factions); Para 16A – suspend/withdraw recognition for defying the MCC; Sec. 29A RPA 1951 – registration by the ECI.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Election Commission cannot deregister a registered party merely because it fails to win seats or its vote share falls.
Reason (R): The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is an Act of Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: under INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002) deregistration is possible only for fraud in obtaining registration, ceasing allegiance to the Constitution or being declared unlawful (the 255th Law Commission Report seeks a limited power). R is false: the 1968 Order is a statutory order of the ECI under the RPA 1951 and Art. 324.

Match List-I (Route to State-party recognition) with List-II (Requirement besides / instead of seats):
List-I | List-II
a. 6% of valid votes in the Assembly election | i. 3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats, whichever is more
b. 6% of valid votes in the Lok Sabha election from the State | ii. 8% of valid votes, no seat needed
c. Assembly seat route | iii. plus 1 Lok Sabha seat
d. Vote-only route | iv. plus 2 Assembly seats
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 6% Assembly votes + 2 Assembly seats; 6% Lok Sabha votes + 1 Lok Sabha seat; 3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats, whichever is more; 8% of valid votes with no seat (not 10%). The fifth route is 1 Lok Sabha seat for every 25 allotted to the State.

Consider the following statements about election symbols:
1. Free symbols are for registered-unrecognised parties and independents; the May 2025 list has 184 symbols.
2. A registered-unrecognised party may get a common symbol if it contests at least 4 Lok Sabha seats or 5% of Assembly seats.
3. Two recognised parties in different States cannot hold the same reserved symbol.
4. The CPI has contested every Lok Sabha election on the same symbol, ears of corn and sickle.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Two are correct (1 and 4). 2 is wrong: the common-symbol condition is at least 2 Lok Sabha seats (or 5% of Assembly seats). 3 is wrong: reserved symbols belong to recognised parties, and two recognised parties in different States may hold the same symbol.

s:
Consider the following statements about the benefits of recognised political parties:
1. The candidate of a recognised party needs only one proposer for nomination, against ten for an RUPP.
2. A recognised party gets two free sets of electoral rolls.
3. A recognised party gets free broadcast time on Doordarshan but not on Akashvani.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: broadcast/telecast time is given on both Akashvani and Doordarshan.

s:
Consider the following statements about registered-unrecognised political parties (RUPPs):
1. An RUPP must contest an election at least once in six years or be delisted.
2. An RUPP must disclose donors giving above Rs 2,000.
3. Donations above Rs 2,000 must come only by cheque or bank transfer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: donor disclosure applies above Rs 20,000; Rs 2,000 is the ceiling for non-cheque donations. Their tax exemption is under Sec. 12 of the Income Tax Act 2025.
